ECT DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
• After your treatment you may feel drowsy and have a problem concentrating.
• Stay at home and rest for the remainder of the day.
• No driving at all during an acute or index ECT series (two or more treatments per week). Cognition and concentration may be
impaired.
• Once in the maintenance/continuation phase of ECT (no more than one treatment per week), do not drive for 24 hours after your
procedure.
• Be cautious about making major decisions while you are undergoing ECT.
• Eat small meals often at first and increase slowly.
• Call the ECT coordinator by dialing 662-3129 for any problems you feel are related to your procedure, or go to the nearest
emergency room.
FOR YOUR NEXT ECT APPOINTMENT:
• Do not have anything to eat or drink after midnight the night prior to your treatment. If you have a later appointment and need
fluids, you may have clear liquids (water, gatorade, apple juice, cranberry juice) up until two hours prior to hour appointment time.
• If you are on a benzodiazepine or anti-seizure medication, do not take this medication after 6P the night prior to your treatment.
• The morning of your treatment, do not take your morning medications unless instructed to do so.
• You should take your scheduled morning cardiac medications and medications for indigestion with a small sip of water two (2)
hours prior to your appointment.
• Remove all head and neck jewelry before coming in for your treatment.
• Keep hair free of all hair products other than shampoo and conditioner.
• Make sure you have arranged for someone to drive you home and that you have someone who can stay with you if needed if you
are confused.
• If you have any questions prior to your scheduled treatment, please call Beth Perry, RN, ECT Coordinator, at 662-3129.

ECT DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
• After your treatment you may feel drowsy and have a problem concentrating.
• Stay at home and rest for the remainder of the day.
• No driving at all during an acute or index ECT series (two or more treatments per week). Cognition and concentration may be
impaired.
• Once in the maintenance/continuation phase of ECT (no more than one treatment per week), do not drive for 24 hours after your
procedure.
• You should not be drinking alcohol while receiving ECT, especially 24 hours prior to your treatment.
• Be cautious about making major decisions while you are undergoing ECT.
• Eat small meals often at first and increase slowly.
• Call the ECT coordinator by dialing 662-3129 for any problems you feel are related to your procedure, or go to the nearest
emergency room.
FOR YOUR NEXT ECT APPOINTMENT:
• Do not have anything to eat or drink after midnight the night prior to your treatment. If you have a later appointment and need
fluids, you may have clear liquids (water, gatorade, apple juice, cranberry juice) up until two hours prior to hour appointment time.
• If you are on a benzodiazepine or anti-seizure medication, do not take this medication after 6P the night prior to your treatment.
• The morning of your treatment, do not take your morning medications unless instructed to do so.
• You should take your scheduled morning cardiac medications and medications for indigestion with a small sip of water two (2)
hours prior to your appointment.
• Remove all head and neck jewelry before coming in for your treatment.
• Keep hair free of all hair products other than shampoo and conditioner.
• Make sure you have arranged for someone to drive you home and that you have someone who can stay with you if needed if you
are confused.
• If you have any questions prior to your scheduled treatment, please call Beth Perry, RN, ECT Coordinator, at 662-3129.

EXAM: ULTRASOUND-GUIDED PERCUTANEOUS RANDOM CORE LIVER BIOPSY
INDICATION: Ultrasound-guided liver biopsy requested. Reactive arthritis. Elevated ALT, AST. Evaluate
for hemochromatosis with quantitative iron evaluation as well.
COMPARISON: Ultrasound 12/23/14.
FINDINGS: Identification and procedure time out were performed. Signed informed consent was obtained.
The biopsy was performed by Dr. Winn with Dr. Brian Alan Perry.
An oblique right intercostal approach was selected. Realtime ultrasound guidance was used throughout the
procedure. Standard sterile preparation and technique were employed. Local anesthesia was obtained with
infusion of 1% lidocaine solution. A
biopsy was performed with coaxial technique with the need for multiple core specimens for the diagnostic
testing requested, per discussion with the Pathology department prior to the procedure. With realtime
ultrasound guidance, a 17-gauge introducer
needle was placed into the right lobe of the liver. A biopsy was performed through that with an 18-gauge
spring loaded automatic core biopsy needle. Two separate 2 cm long cores were obtained. These were
placed together in a single container of
formalin and submitted for histopathologic evaluation and quantitative iron evaluation. The biopsy
needle was removed and stylet was placed within the coaxial needle. After approximately 3 minutes the
stylet was removed and revealed no bleeding through
the coaxial needle. The coaxial needle was then removed. Postbiopsy imaging showed no evidence of
hemorrhage or immediate perihepatic hematoma.
The site was cleansed and a band-aid was applied. The patient was placed in right lateral decubitus
recumbency and brought to the radiology nursing area for postbiopsy observation with orders placed in the
electronic medical record. Specimen was
submitted for diagnostic testing as ordered.
IMPRESSION: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous random core liver biopsy performed. Details above.
